title: Kuro-chan and the Dark Swordsman
text: “Yeah. So the Wave really is coming tomorrow, huh?”

I registered with the Dragon Hourglass and confirmed the Wave’s arrival time. Our forces were more than ready to make tomorrow’s Wave an easy win. First priority was evacuating the Filolial-samas, then helping Father and the others take down the Wave’s boss, the Chimera. According to Father and the others from the previous loop, the key to shaping Filo-tan lay with the Wave’s boss, after all. It suddenly occurred to me—could this Wave be connected to the world where Rival was? …If I dawdled about, Rival might show up, indeed. Since it was the night before the decisive battle, I decided to ask Older Sister to arrange a delightful night for Father, so he could finally graduate from virginity.
“Motoyasu-kun?”
“Motoyasu-sama, you have such a dignified expression.”
“Hmm?”
“I thought it was too quiet.”
“Aren’t you thinking of something strange?”
Yuki-chan looked at me dreamily, while in contrast, the mongrel lizardman and rabbit man raised strange complaints.
“No problem at all. Face tomorrow’s Wave without fear, I say.”
“Yeah. It’ll be fine, since everyone’s here.”
“Yeah… but…”
“That was a troubling silence. Something strange… I can only pray you won’t do anything odd just because it’s the night before the decisive battle.”

Incidentally, when I asked Older Sister for help, Father summoned me that night and scolded me instead. Whatever would it take for Father to finally graduate from virginity? Kind Father seemed outwardly interested in such matters, yet was actually terribly bashful, indeed. Not so much cowardly as simply shallow in his outward interest while lacking any real depth to it… Perhaps this was where he overlapped with Ark, who claimed to have no gender at all. Surely Father would wholeheartedly affirm that friendship between men and women could exist. Of course, I was also in the affirming camp, but I also believed romance was important. One ought to respect both, I say. Ark had said something about being like a dragon’s relative, but that was clearly a different matter here. Looking at Rival and her kin, the difference was obvious—those creatures were lumps of lust incarnate, indeed. I would never forgive that. Just as I was thinking such things, I heard Itsuki’s voice.
“Oh? Isn’t that Motoyasu-san and Naofumi-… san over there?”
Just as I remembered, Itsuki was there with his companions, without the Crimson Swine in tow.
“What’s with you two? Was there some kind of gathering?”
Just then, Ren appeared too.
“Waah.”
Kuro-chan spotted Ren and reacted with a little peep, her eyes sparkling as she closed the distance toward him.
“It’s not really anything in particular, but…”
“You caused quite a stir, after all… I figured you’d left the country for good, but you’re still around, huh.”
“Well, sort of.”
“I see. We haven’t crossed paths since then, but… looks like Naofumi’s gathered a few companions of his own.”
Ren looked at me and Yuki-chan, then shifted his gaze to the mongrel lizardman and rabbit man behind Father… and finally toward Kuro-chan, who was steadily closing in.
“A winged… demi-human?”
“Dark Swordsman~”
“What is this thing?”
“That’s Kuro-chan, I say.”
“Yup, Kuro’s name is Kuro.”
“…I see.”

Despite everything, Ren seemed to have taken quite a liking to the Filolial-sama’s appearance. Those wings on her back seemed to strike a chord with Ren’s sensibilities, after all. Back when wings had sprouted on his own back, he’d put off having them removed, indeed.
“Hey, what’s your name~? Come join Kuro in the destiny battle of the Dark Holy Hero <Black Chronicle>, and let’s take on the fight to stop the Catastrophe of ruinous fate~”

Ren, his face painted with a single character’s worth of confusion, turned his gaze toward Father and me. His attitude could’ve been read either as a plea for help, or as someone who’d just found a friend to talk to.
“Looks like Kuro-chan’s taken a liking to you, Ren. Mind being her conversation partner for a bit?”
“Wh— wait a second, Naofumi!”
“Kuro-chan. That person’s name is Ren Amaki, and he’s the Sword Hero.”
“Got it~. So Ren’s the Dark Swordsman, the Dark Holy Hero~ Talk with Kuro and awaken to your dark <Destiny>~”
“Hmph! That kind of act isn’t my taste.”
Ren crossed his arms and turned his back.
“Waah.”
Kuro-chan’s eyes sparkled even brighter, I say. Playing along with the conversation here apparently wasn’t the sort of development Kuro-chan preferred.
“Well, when you think ‘hero,’ swords do come to mind. I get why Kuro-chan would be drawn to that.”
“Hmph.”
“Father, what about me, I wonder?”
“A hero with a spear feels more like historical fiction or some fantasy war chronicle, I’d say?”
“Romance of the Three Kingdoms, indeed!”
“Well… that does have a bit of an idealized-drama feel to it, but…”
Itsuki watched this exchange with a slight furrow of his brow as he drew closer.
“Naofumi-san. Even after everything that happened, with rumors flying around the country, you’ve managed to gain companions willing to travel with you.”
“I suppose.”
Father glanced at the mongrel lizardman and rabbit man before nodding.
The mongrel lizardman seemed to agree with a faint sigh mixed in, while the rabbit man eyed Itsuki suspiciously.
Silence reigned between Father and Itsuki both.
“Hey~ Dark Swordsman~”
“Don’t just slap weird nicknames on me!”

In the background, Ren was frolicking about with Kuro-chan. Quite the peaceful sight. Thanks to Kuro-chan, the bad atmosphere felt like it was being purified, I say. Now then, I knew what needed doing—I’d take on the role of moderator.
“Did you and Itsuki come to give your companions a Class Up, Ren?”
“That’s… right, but.”
“You two are different, then?”
Incidentally, both Ren and Itsuki had companions waiting behind them.
“…First we’re just scouting things out.”
“Oh? You don’t know?”
The mongrel lizardman and rabbit man moved to answer Ren’s question.
“Know what?”
“In this country, demi-humans and beastmen aren’t granted permission for Class Up.”
“Oh, really…”
At the rabbit man’s answer, both Ren and Itsuki’s eyebrows shot up.
“The Wave’s approaching, isn’t it? Why not allow it? This is exactly the sort of time a hero’s companions would need it.”
“No, no, isn’t the reason permission’s been denied because of Naofumi-san? In the sense that he hasn’t earned the country’s trust. It also looks like he’s trying to make young children fight.”
“Well, well, is that how a hero fighting for the sake of the world ought to be treated? For the one making the request to act this way—doesn’t that show quite a bit of contempt for the world?”
The rabbit man shot back swiftly at Itsuki’s reply. Quite the provocation, indeed.
“Besides, Yuki-chan and Kuro-chan are my Filolial-samas to begin with, I say.”

They were my companions, not Father’s. At present, the ones we had with us were Yuki-chan and Kuro-chan with me, while Father had the mongrel lizardman and rabbit man, plus Wolf waiting outside the building. So the claim about making children fight didn’t hold up.
“What did you say Iwatani-sama did?”
“Do you all know? Naofumi-san has a prior record of attempted rape.”
“Itsuki!”
Father, unable to contain himself, glared. The mongrel lizardman let out a sigh. Ren, meanwhile, didn’t seem to have time to sigh, his attention fixed on Kuro-chan as she kept clinging to him.

“If he had that much push in him, it’d be one thing. The Spear Hero’s been badgering the Shield Hero to graduate from virginity so persistently it’s almost annoying. I’d honestly like him to just get some experience already and settle down.”
What did he say?! This is a matter of great importance, I say! Hey, lizard, what’s the meaning of this?!
“Shion!”
“That much is fine, isn’t it… honestly, well, I can’t say I don’t get why he’d go limp with all that pestering.”
“Iwatani-sama, rape?”

Beside the mongrel lizardman, who was trying to calm the furious Father, the rabbit man answered Itsuki. Sensing the mood, Yuki-chan was practically itching to jump in too. No, Yuki-chan! If she voiced her honest agreement here, she’d only earn a scolding from Father, so she had to hold back, indeed. I took Yuki-chan’s hand and pressed a finger to my lips, signaling her to hold it in. The rabbit man laughed so hard he clutched his stomach.
